transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-12
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Miguel Santos (CISO), Dana Lee (VP Eng), Ravi Patel (Platform Lead)

Summary (auto): Security posture discovery focusing on compliance artifacts and technical integration points for Private/Dedicated deployment. Next steps: share SOC2/ISO docs, schedule KMS deep dive, provide pricing/pilot scope.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex Chen from Redwood Inference, I'm the AE on the account, with me is Priya our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Miguel: Good, thanks Alex. Miguel here, CISO at Peregrine. We only have about 50 minutes, so want to run through our security checklist.
[00:15] Alex: Perfect, that's the plan. Priya do you want to say quick hello?
[00:18] Priya: Hi all, Priya Nair. I'll focus on the architecture and integration bits, e.g., VPC/private, KMS flows, RBAC.
[00:25] Dana: Dana Lee, VP eng. Main concern is data residency and latency; also curious about Dedicated vs Hosted costs.
[00:31] Ravi: Ravi Patel, platform lead. I'll own the technical follow ups.

[00:35] Alex: Great. Miguel, maybe start with your big picture requirements? SOC2 or ISO requirements? retention windows?
[00:42] Miguel: Sure. We're SOC 2 Type II in flight, likely closing in Q1 but we need to validate vendor controls. ISO 27001 is also relevant. Questions: do you have current certs, how do you handle encryption keys, do you support SSO with SAML, and how are audit logs surfaced?
[00:57] Alex: Good questions. We have a SOC 2 Type II report and an ISO summary — I'll share the artifacts. For keys we support customer-managed KMS in Private deployments and AWS KMS integrations on Dedicated; on Hosted we use provider-managed keys but we offer envelope encryption and options for bring-your-own-key via partner KMS in some regions.
[01:20] Miguel: When you say "provider-managed" — is that Redwood owning the key material? That's a hard no for a lot of our data, we need customer control for certain tokens.
[01:29] Priya: Right, so for Private (VPC / on-prem) you can bring your KMS/HSM and we integrate over standard APIs — we document the KMS key rotation and access control. With Dedicated we can do a customer KMS in the same cloud account or a cross-account KMS setup; Hosted uses our managed key unless you opt into the enterprise KMS add-on.
[01:48] Ravi: Are those cross-account roles IAM-based? We need to know network flow — we run in AWS, EKS, with strict egress.
[01:55] Priya: Yes, it's cross-account IAM roles and VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on the option. For egress-restricted environments we support VPC endpoints and peered VPCs; we'll send diagrams.

[02:10] Dana: About SSO — we use Okta and AzureAD. We need SAML 2.0 support and SCIM for user provisioning.
[02:18] Alex: We support SAML SSO and SCIM. There's a little bit of variation in the setup between Hosted and Private — Hosted has a simple tenant option in Console, Private has SAML config plus SAML assertion mapping into our RBAC model.
[02:34] Miguel: Can we map SAML groups to RBAC roles? We want least privilege and just-in-time admin.
[02:40] Priya: Yep, group-to-role mapping is supported. You can map Okta groups to Redwood roles, and we honor attribute mappings. There's also audit trails for administrative actions.

[02:52] Ravi: Audit logs — how are they surfaced? We need immutable logs for at least 12 months and the ability to forward to our SIEM.
[02:59] Priya: Audit logs are available via API and can be shipped to your S3 or pushed to a SIEM via a connector. In Dedicated/Private you can retain logs in your environment; Hosted we retain per plan but can stream to your endpoints. We'll share retention matrix.
[03:15] Miguel: Retention is critical. For some data we need seven years, but for logs 2-3 years is typical. Does your export preserve PII redaction?
[03:25] Alex: We redact some PII in logs by default but we can customize what is captured in Dedicated/Private. We'll include documentation on PII handling.

[03:38] Dana: Encryption at rest — default AES256? Are DBs encrypted? Are backups encrypted?
[03:44] Priya: All at-rest data is AES-256 with KMS-managed keys. Backups are encrypted as well. With customer-managed KMS we rotate keys per your policy.

[03:55] Miguel: Key rotation — do you support automatic rotation and key archiving policies? Also, HSM support?
[04:03] Priya: We support automatic rotation if you're managing keys in AWS KMS. For HSM we integrate with customer HSMs in Private or on-prem installs; you can require HSM-backed keys for signing.

[04:18] Alex: One note on terminology — sometimes our docs say "Redwood Dedicated" or "Redwood Private" and the auto transcription might show "Red wood Dedicated" — apologies in advance in case our docs look odd.

[04:28] Miguel: (laughs) that's fine. On certifications — you said you have SOC2 Type II. Can you share the control mapping and any third-party pen test results?
[04:36] Alex: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II report and a third-party penetration test summary. We'll provide a control mapping spreadsheet showing how controls map to customer questions.

[04:48] Ravi: Network isolation when running Dedicated — are GPUs in customer tenancy or shared?
[04:54] Priya: Dedicated is reserved capacity in our infrastructure but with tenancy isolation and logical separation. For full customer tenancy we have Private on-prem packages. We can detail the isolation model — some folks want physically dedicated hardware, others are fine with reserved pools.

[05:12] Miguel: Data flows — where does the user prompt data persist? Are prompts stored, for how long, and are they used for model training?
[05:20] Alex: By default Hosted does not use customer prompts to train models; we have a policy and contract language. Retention varies by deployment: Hosted has configurable retention windows, Dedicated typically allows you to opt-in/out of retention, Private you control retention entirely. We'll send the retention policy table.

[05:42] Dana: We have to be strict: no training on sensitive prompts, and retention of raw prompts must be deletable on request. Can you support delete/gdpr?
[05:51] Priya: Yes, we support data deletion requests and retention controls; in dedicated/private you can configure auto-delete rules. For Hosted we provide APIs to delete and a retention UI.

[06:05] Miguel: Logging integrity — can logs be WORM or appended to an external S3 with object lock? We might need tamper-evident logs.
[06:13] Priya: We support shipping to customer-owned S3 with AWS Object Lock for immutable storage and we can integrate with your SIEM for tamper detection.

[06:25] Ravi: How about incident response and breach notification SLA?
[06:29] Alex: Our standard enterprise contract includes breach notification timelines; typically 72 hours for confirmed incidents, with a designated Redwood security contact. We'll share the SOC2 incident section and the contract language.

[06:41] Miguel: Does Redwood do red team exercises or have summaries from external tests?
[06:46] Priya: We have periodic pen tests and a red team summary; we can provide a sanitized report and remediation notes.

[06:56] Dana: On RBAC — do you support fine-grained token scopes for API keys? We don't want full-admin keys floating around.
[07:03] Priya: Yes, API keys can be scoped and time-limited; you can also use short-lived tokens via SSO and exchange. We support scoped roles per model/route.

[07:16] Miguel: For compliance we need audit of who invoked what model and input/output hashes. Are outputs logged? How do we avoid storing PII in outputs?
[07:25] Alex: We can log metadata and input/output hashes; the actual content capture is configurable. For PII we recommend token-level redaction and a policy to not persist outputs for sensitive routes.

[07:40] Ravi: Any restrictions on on-prem hardware? Our infra team wants to know GPU support, drivers, and supported OS.
[07:47] Priya: For on-prem we support common Nvidia GPUs (A10/A100/etc) and provide a supported list with driver versions; we have an on-prem deployment guide.

[07:58] Dana: SLAs — uptime and latency guarantees differ by Dedicated vs Hosted?
[08:03] Alex: Hosted has best-effort and published SLOs; Dedicated has SLA-backed targets, depending on commit. Private has negotiated SLAs. We'll include the SLA matrix.

[08:16] Miguel: Encryption in transit — TLS 1.2/1.3? Mutual TLS option?
[08:20] Priya: TLS 1.2/1.3 supported; mutual TLS is available for private peering and some Dedicated configurations.

[08:32] Alex: Quick flag — customer-managed KMS in Dedicated means Redwood does not have access to plaintext keys; we only get ciphertext. That tends to satisfy most customers who need key control.

[08:44] Miguel: Helpful. On legal — do you sign standard DPA and include subprocessors list?
[08:49] Alex: Yes, DPA and subprocessor list provided. We'll send the latest DPA and a link to the subprocessor page.

[09:00] Ravi: Performance benchmarking — we might want to run a throughput test during pilot. How do we run benchmarks without exposing data?
[09:07] Priya: We can run synthetic workloads and provide tooling for the pilot. For Private you can run tests inside your VPC. For Hosted we provide a sandbox and obfuscated data patterns.

[09:20] Dana: Cost controls — token billing and audit for usage per route? We need per-team budget caps.
[09:26] Alex: Console provides per-token cost breakdowns and per-route/ per-team usage caps. You can configure per-route model limits and alerts.

[09:36] Miguel: Anything about cryptographic attestations or FIPS 140-2?
[09:40] Priya: We support FIPS-compliant modules via customer-managed HSMs; Redwood's hosted keys may not be FIPS. We'll note that in the doc.

[09:50] Alex: Ok, small check: are there any blockers for starting a pilot?
[09:54] Miguel: We need the SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration details, plus the retention matrix. Also, approval from procurement for the pilot.
[10:03] Alex: We'll send SOC2, ISO summary, pen-test summary, onboarding docs, and a pilot proposal. Priya will own the technical deep dive.

[10:10] Ravi: One more — audit log schema, fields, and how to correlate request IDs with application logs.
[10:16] Priya: We'll include the schema and examples. We emit request IDs, model IDs, route IDs, and user IDs for correlation.

[10:26] Miguel: Ok. Can you also confirm no training on prompts for Hosted? We've had vendors auto-ingest data before.
[10:32] Alex: Confirmed — Hosted does not use customer data for model training by default and it's in our contract; we can provide contractual language.

[10:40] Dana: Last question — can we get a demo of Private deployment install and the KMS handshake?
[10:45] Priya: Yes, we'll schedule an install walkthrough in the technical deep dive. We'll show the KMS handshake and the VPC peering steps.

[10:54] Alex: Great, recap of next steps: I'll send compliance pack and pricing; Priya will schedule technical deep dive with Ravi; Miguel will send regs and retention requirements. Everyone good?
[11:05] Miguel: Yep, that's good. Thanks all.
[11:08] Dana: Thanks.
[11:10] Alex: Thanks folks, we'll follow up by email.

[11:15] (meeting ends)

Notes: Transcript contains occasional ASR artifacts (e.g., "Red wood" for Redwood, "K V cache" for KV cache, "SAMEL" for SAML). Links referenced in next steps will be included in the follow-up email.
